data.interpretation: The KPI has two parts. The main objective is the town-wide count of deliveries that meet both promised windows (pickup within 120 s of the order, delivery within 120 s of pickup), which maps to on_time_deliveries. The second sentence is a fairness floor: no single company's customers should get badly worse service, which maps most directly to min_company_on_time_rate. 'Badly' is not quantified, so any threshold is a human judgement. The 120 s windows are part of DELIVERY_SLA, a contract. They are a fixed yardstick for this KPI and must not be changed as a way to improve the metrics; any SLA change needs a human decision.

options.label: Maximize town-wide on-time deliveries, with a floor on the worst company's on-time rate

goals.text: Primary: number of orders delivered within both promised windows across the town (higher is better).
Monitor: on-time rate of the worst-served company must not deteriorate.
Monitor: orders left undelivered at period end, so on-time counts are not raised by abandoning hard orders.

guards.text: Every company keeps at least 70% of its deliveries on time (provisional reading of 'not kept waiting badly'; calibrate against baseline).

options.note: Closest to the literal KPI: volume first, fairness as a hard floor. The 0.7 threshold is a placeholder for the human to set, ideally relative to the measured baseline.

options.label: Maximize the worst company's on-time rate, with town-wide volume as a monitored goal

goals.text: Primary: on-time rate of the worst-served company (higher is better).
Monitor: town-wide on-time deliveries must not drop.
Monitor: undelivered orders at period end.

guards.text: Gap between the best and worst company's on-time rate stays within 20 percentage points (provisional).

options.note: Puts the fairness sentence first. It may accept amendments that help the weakest company even when town-wide gains are small. Choose this if the second sentence is the binding concern.

options.label: Maximize town-wide on-time deliveries; read 'kept waiting badly' as late or abandoned orders

guards.text: No order is left undelivered at period end (provisional; customers never served are the worst case of waiting).

options.note: Reads 'badly' as orders that are very late or never delivered, not as a per-company rate. It does not directly protect a specific company, so fairness is only monitored.

concerns: 'Kept waiting badly' is not quantified. It could mean a per-company on-time rate floor, a cap on the rate gap between companies, or no abandoned or very late orders. The guard thresholds (0.7, 0.2, 0) are placeholders the human must confirm.

on_time_deliveries is a count. Optimizing it alone can reward rules that let the hard or remote orders of one company go unfinished or late, which goes against the fairness sentence. For that reason unfinished and min_company_on_time_rate are monitored.

Maximizing the town-wide total and protecting the worst company can conflict. Road rules that favor throughput, such as letting busy robots hold a road longer, may push one company's on-time rate down.

With only 2 robots per company, per-company rates are noisy. A strict guard on min_company_on_time_rate or on_time_rate_gap may reject good amendments because of random variation unless the measurement covers enough orders.

Both metrics depend on the 120 s windows in DELIVERY_SLA. Relaxing the SLA would inflate on-time counts without real improvement, so the SLA must be treated as fixed under this KPI. Any change to it is a contract decision for the human.
